The First Shadow, now an integral part of the ST canon, is an absolute must-see for all enthusiasts, and it will certainly inspire some of the uninitiated to binge the original (mission accomplished, Netflix).

Immersive, heartfelt, and exhilarating, First Shadow is a must-see spectacle for the Stranger Things obsessive as much as it is for the theater aficionado who wants to see the medium pushed to new heights.

'First Shadow' also offers substance, in the form of a cleverly constructed story that director Stephen Daldry and his vibrant young cast make compelling even for those of us who haven't watched 'Stranger Things' faithfully, or at all.
The show is a proudly brazen piece of brand extension, with the familiar title card of the TV show opening the production, much to the delight of fans watching on.

Personally, though, after seeing “Stranger Things: The First Shadow,” I had nightmares about mega-corporations taking over Broadway and providing us with sub-par theatrical product.

Broadway may be open to big-budget extensions of TV properties—expect “Squid Game: Origins” any day now, along with a previously announced “Game of Thrones” prequel—but storytelling, not brand loyalty, is what separates genuine drama from glorified fan service.

cn.t: Critics are split on this spectacle-heavy prequel: technical wizardry and special effects dazzle, but many find the three-hour runtime bloated and the story confusing for non-superfans, despite strong performances from its young cast.
